config.title: Beelitz-Heilstätten from Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Opening days, trains, tickets and building tours for a Beelitz-Heilstätten trip from Berlin this autumn and winter.

items.q: How do I get from Berlin to Beelitz-Heilstätten?
items.a: Take the **RE7** to Beelitz-Heilstätten station; the park entrance is a five-minute walk. Until **12 December 2026** the RE7 starts at **Berlin-Charlottenburg**, so take the S-Bahn there first. From Hauptbahnhof the trip takes about 50 minutes.

Partly. It is open daily **10:00 to 16:00 from 2 to 15 November** and on 21 and 22 November, but **closed from 16 to 20 and from 23 to 26 November**. From **27 November** it opens only in the evening for the ZEITREISE light trail.

items.q: Can you go inside the buildings at Beelitz-Heilstätten?
items.a: Only on a **guided tour**. Entering the fenced buildings on your own is trespassing. Tours last 60 or 90 minutes, cost **10 to 17 euros** on top of the park ticket, need a hard hat and are mostly from age 12.

items.q: Are there tours in English at Beelitz-Heilstätten?
items.a: Not as public tours. The scheduled tours run **in German**; an English tour is only possible as a **private group booking** by email with the operator, Baum & Zeit.

items.q: How much does the Beelitz-Heilstätten treetop walk cost?
items.a: **17 euros** for adults until the end of October, 12 euros for ages 7 to 17, free under 7. From November the **winter tariff** is 13.50 euros for adults and 10 euros for children. The ZEITREISE evening trail is **19 euros online** or 23 euros at the door.

items.q: Does the Berlin ABC ticket cover Beelitz-Heilstätten?
items.a: No. Beelitz-Heilstätten is outside the Berlin ABC zone. A VBB single from Berlin costs **6.30 euros** each way and a 24-hour ticket 12 euros; the **Deutschlandticket** covers the whole trip.

An evening **light and sound trail** of about 90 minutes through the park, some of the old buildings and up onto the treetop walk, starting **27 November 2026**. Entry is from 16:00 in timed slots, and slots are limited, so book online.
No. Dogs are not allowed in the park, on the treetop walk or on the tours.
